result:
The proposed answer of 22 is wrong, because a simple monotonicity argument gives a lower bound of 25.

**Lower bound from $R(K_4, K_5) = 25$:** The graph $K_5 - e$ contains a $K_4$. So any 2-coloring with no blue $K_4$ also has no blue $K_5 - e$. Since $R(K_5, K_4) = 25$, there is a 2-coloring of $K_{24}$ with no red $K_5$ and no blue $K_4$. That coloring has no red $K_5$ and no blue $K_5 - e$, so $R(K_5, K_5 - e) \geq 25 > 22$.

The proposed solution also has other errors. $R(K_4, K_4 - e)$ is $10$, not $11$. The "verification" of the upper bound is only an appeal to unspecified "combinatorial arguments," so it does not establish anything. The lower-bound claim of a valid coloring of $K_{21}$ is also not justified, and it is already contradicted by the coloring above, which works on 24 vertices.

I can't confirm the exact value of $R(K_5, K_5 - e)$ from memory, but whatever it is, it is at least 25, so 22 cannot be correct.

VERDICT: REJECT
